+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                 ROMAN RHETORIC — LANDSCAPE                       |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
|                                                                  |
|  CICERO (106-43 BCE)                                             |
|  De Inventione (early): theory of argument discovery            |
|  De Oratore (55 BCE): the mature synthesis; the ideal orator   |
|  Orator (46 BCE): the orator's style across three levels        |
|  Brutus (46 BCE): history of Roman oratory                      |
|  The Philippics: his political speeches (killed him)            |
|                                                                  |
|  QUINTILIAN (c. 35-100 CE)                                      |
|  Institutio Oratoria: the complete education of an orator       |
|  12 books; comprehensive; the ideal orator is also a good man  |
|                                                                  |
|  ROMAN FORENSIC PRACTICE                                         |
|  The Roman courts: advocacy as political career                  |
|  The stasis theory: finding the point at issue                  |
|  Actio (delivery) as core political performance                  |
|                                                                  |
|  THE LEGACY                                                      |
|  Medieval ars praedicandi (preaching manuals)                   |
|  Renaissance humanism (studia humanitatis)                      |
|  Jesuit education (rhetorical training)                         |
|  Modern business communication (trace the lineage)             |
+------------------------------------------------------------------+
